messages:
Priya: quick q — we're trying to wire a small kv-cache sidecar (inside payments svc) that needs to decrypt config blobs with our customer KMS key. using IRSA for k8s SA. wondering best practice: key policy vs aws_kms_grant vs inline role policy. here's the relevant snippets, any red flags?

Priya: terraform snippet:
```hcl
resource \"aws_iam_role\" \"payments_cache_sa_role\" {
  name = \"payments-cache-sa-role\"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_sa.json
}

resource \"aws_kms_key\" \"customer_key\" {
  description = \"customer data key\"
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.kms_key_policy.json
}
```

Priya: k8s SA annotation:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: payments-cache-sa
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/payments-cache-sa-role
```

Priya: current plan gave decrypt errors from the sidecar: "AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/payments-cache-sa-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource"

Alex: ok classic. two ways: (1) put the IAM principal (role) into the KMS key policy principal list OR (2) keep key policy strict + create aws_kms_grant for the role. grants avoid editing key policy if you want short-lived access. also ensure conditions (SourceAccount/SourceArn) if you want to limit to the role session.

Sam: small note — if the key is multi-tenant (customer-owned) and you don't want to touch the key policy for each role, prefer aws_kms_grant with constraint on encryption_context maybe. grants get auto-removed on role deletion? they persist until revoked though.

Maria: +1 on grant. We had a weird case where EKS pods assumed role with session name longer than 64 chars and our key policy condition on aws:SourceArn didn't match. Better to use SourceAccount + SourceArn wildcard: \"arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/payments-cache-sa-role/*\"

Priya: thanks. if we do aws_kms_grant, do we need to include kms:Decrypt in the role's inline policy too?

Alex: the grant gives KMS-level permission; IAM policy is still evaluated for identity-based permissions for other services. For KMS calls, KMS evaluates key policy and grants to allow. You can have minimal IAM policy (sts:AssumeRole) but the grant must reference the role principal.

Sam: here's a sample terraform for grant we used before:
```hcl
resource \"aws_kms_grant\" \"payments_cache_grant\" {
  name = \"payments-cache-grant\"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.customer_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.payments_cache_sa_role.arn
  operations = [\"Decrypt\", \"GenerateDataKey\"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      \"service\" = \"payments-cache\"
    }
  }
}
```

Maria: also be careful about cross-account keys. If the key is in another account, you must update key policy in the key's account (can't create a grant from a different account unless using GrantTokens and proper permissions).

Priya: good catch — key is in the same account. one more — our sidecar uses the AWS SDK in-process and calls GenerateDataKey then Decrypt. any session name -> anything special?

Alex: no special session name needed, but if your key policy or conditions check aws:PrincipalOrgID or SourceArn make sure the session's arn matches the pattern. EKS IRSA creates assumed-role/session format. I usually test with:
```bash
aws sts get-caller-identity --output text
# run inside pod via awscli sidecar
```

Priya: ran that inside pod, output: 
"arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/payments-cache-sa-role/i-eks-012345" — looks normal.

Sam: one more ops tip: if you create a grant, you might need to schedule a rotate/redeploy if grant not picked up? usually immediate. but if policy caching on SDK side, restart sidecar.

infra-bot: terraform plan finished for module.payments (diag) — 2 additions (aws_kms_grant.payments_cache_grant, aws_iam_role.payments_cache_sa_role)

Priya: thanks all. i'll try aws_kms_grant approach with encryption_context subset and wildcard SourceArn in the key policy fallback. will ping when plan hits staging. :thumbsup:

Alex: lmk if you want a quick pair to review the grant tf — took us 10m last time.

Priya: appreciate it, tagging you @Alex when ready.
